name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: Large pharma at a reasonable valuation, with a new-drug pipeline building to offset Keytruda's patent expiry, and the stock is above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: Revenue loss after Keytruda's patent expiry, and the upcoming quarterly report.

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: A fee-based pipeline and natural-gas-liquids network with rising volumes from the Permian basin; the stock is at a new high.
targets.risks: Energy concentration and lower drilling activity if commodity prices fall.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: Steel prices are supported by tariffs and rising US demand, and the stock is up 14% in a month to near its high.
targets.risks: Steel prices peaking or tariff policy changes.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: The leading endpoint-security platform, with fast growth in recurring revenue and strong momentum (+85% over 12 months, 50% above its 200-day average).
targets.risks: A very high valuation, which this week's Fortinet sell-off shows the market is punishing in security stocks.

targets.name: Marathon Petroleum
targets.thesis: Refining margins are very high, and the company returns a lot of capital to shareholders through buybacks, backed by strong cash flow.
targets.risks: Refining margins could fall back to normal levels from their current peak.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: Since its split into separate companies, the remaining DuPont is a more focused electronics and industrial materials business, with strong price momentum near its highs.
targets.risks: A cyclical slowdown in industrial and electronics demand.

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: A recovery in genetic-sequencing demand and better profit margins are driving earnings up; the stock is within 1.3% of its high.
targets.risks: Competition from cheaper sequencing rivals and possible China or tariff headlines.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: Demand for data storage driven by AI and a shift toward all-flash systems are lifting margins, with strong momentum.
targets.risks: Hardware-stock sentiment is turning, as STX and DELL have already pulled back.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker that is paying down debt and buying back shares, with steady momentum at its highs.
targets.risks: Price erosion in generic drugs and manufacturing compliance problems at its plants.

targets.name: Valero Energy
targets.thesis: Q3 EPS of $23.90 at near-record refinery use; the 10% weekly drop looks like profit-taking, not a broken thesis.
targets.risks: Refining margins normalizing, and overlap with MPC.

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: Its testing and measurement equipment benefits from spending on AI data centers, 6G wireless and defense, and the stock is still above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: Momentum is fading (-6.8% this month, only 5.7% above the 200-day average), so a deeper slide would trigger a review.

targets.name: Fortinet
targets.thesis: Q3 beat with billings up 29%, and full-year guidance was raised for the third time this year; the 26% drop looks like a valuation reset, not a change in the business.
targets.risks: The firewall upgrade wave may be peaking, and stocks often keep drifting lower for weeks after a gap down on earnings.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: A steady fee-based wealth-management business, plus a recovery in investment banking deal activity.
targets.risks: The stock is below its 200-day average and 17% under its high; weak markets would hurt its fee income.

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
